A customer says they have used Extend for over a year and have been very happy with the product and the accuracy of its data extraction.

One commenter called it "the most confusing pricing page I've ever seen." Different options use different amounts of credits and have different costs per credit. They questioned how many degrees of freedom are really needed to represent API cost.
Another user asked what "performance optimized vs cost optimized" means on the pricing page, and whether these are different SLAs or different APIs.

A user said a starter plan of $300+ for startups seems to be a missed opportunity. It could be a high barrier for startups trying the product. They said the product solves a good problem but the pricing seems too high.
One user recommends companies keep it simple and use n8n with Gemini for OCR instead. They claim you would save money and still get 90%+ of the functionality of products like Extend.
A skeptic noted that the 'AI native' OCR/IDP space is already saturated. They pointed to LlamaIndex and many other document orchestration frameworks as alternatives to an end-to-end vendor.

A user of datalab.to (for markdown conversion and some extraction) said they would be interested in replacing it with Extend. However, they were unsure what new capabilities switching would actually open up.

A developer said Extend's open-source UI kit was exactly what they needed for DOCX and XLSX previews in their app. They had planned server-side conversion to PDF because good rendering libraries were lacking.
A user said the UI kit looks clean and works fine but needs optimization. On the landing page, clicking 'Type' in the schema builder example took 1–2 seconds to open a popover on a MacBook Pro M4.

Another user reported that the Extend UI home page heavily lags on an M3 Pro MacBook and suggested lazy loading the components. A second user said the 'Layout blocks' component consumes tons of CPU when scrolling.
While testing the Excel viewer, a user found that the documented 'Search across sheets and cell ranges' feature could not be triggered. The browser's own search also could not find cell contents.

Critics complained that Extend's document UI components are React-only rather than web components, and that the site never states they are React. One user also found Next.js dependencies in the repo's package.json and components.

A developer prototyping bounding boxes on pdf.js called Extend's bounding box demos 'decent'. A developer building a local AI document workflow tool said seeing parsed output without opening Word or PowerPoint is a huge leap.
